payload.task_text:
The HR leadership team wants a comprehensive employee engagement analysis that combines data warehouse insights with new survey instruments and a knowledge base entry. There is a PDF called HR_Engagement_Policy.pdf in the workspace that outlines the company's engagement strategy and target scores by department. There is also a JSON file called engagement_targets.json with numeric targets for each metric. Please read both files first to understand the policy context and targets.

Start by querying the employee data warehouse to get department-level statistics. For each of the 7 departments, calculate the average job satisfaction score, average performance rating, average work-life balance score, and the total employee count. Round all averages to 2 decimal places and sort alphabetically by department.

Next, compute an engagement index for each department. The engagement index is calculated as the weighted average of the three metrics: job satisfaction contributes 40 percent of the weight, work-life balance contributes 35 percent, and performance rating contributes 25 percent. Round this index to 2 decimal places.

Using the command line, write and run a Python script that reads in these department metrics and computes additional analytics. The script should determine which department has the highest engagement index, which has the lowest, the overall company average engagement index, and classify each department as either Above Average or Below Average relative to the company mean. Compute the overall company average as the arithmetic mean of the seven department engagement indices (the rounded values computed in the previous step). Save the script output to a file called engagement_analysis_output.txt in the workspace.

Create a survey form titled "Employee Engagement Survey" with exactly 5 questions. Question 1 asks how satisfied the respondent is with their current role, offering a rating from 1 to 10. Question 2 asks about work-life balance satisfaction with options Very Satisfied, Satisfied, Neutral, Dissatisfied, and Very Dissatisfied. Question 3 asks about career growth opportunities with options Excellent, Good, Fair, and Poor. Question 4 asks how supportive their direct manager is, offering a rating from 1 to 5. Question 5 asks whether they would recommend the company as a great place to work with options Yes, Maybe, and No. The Google Forms tools create only two question types: single-choice multiple choice questions and open text questions. Build all five questions with these two types; for example, the two rating questions can be single-choice multiple choice questions whose options are the numeric scale values (1 through 10, or 1 through 5).

Create exactly one page in the knowledge base titled "HR Engagement Dashboard" that contains a summary of the department statistics including the department names, employee counts, and engagement indices.

Create an Excel file called Employee_Engagement_Report.xlsx in the workspace with three sheets. The first sheet should be called "Department_Scores" with columns Department, Avg_Satisfaction, Avg_Performance, Avg_Work_Life_Balance, Employee_Count, and Engagement_Index. Each row represents one department sorted alphabetically. The second sheet should be called "Survey_Design" with columns Question_Number, Question_Text, and Response_Type listing the 5 survey questions. The third sheet should be called "Action_Items" with columns Priority, Department, and Recommendation. Include one action item row for each department, where the priority is High for departments below the company average engagement index and Medium for those above. The recommendation should mention the specific area where that department scores lowest among the three metrics. Write all numeric values into the spreadsheet as literal numbers, not Excel formulas.

Finally, send an email to hr-leadership@company.com with the subject "Employee Engagement Analysis Report" and a body that summarizes the key findings including which department scored highest and lowest on the engagement index.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use two dependency waves. The main agent dynamically reads HR_Engagement_Policy.pdf and engagement_targets.json first and freezes the literal weights 0.40 satisfaction, 0.35 work-life balance, 0.25 performance.

Wave 1 — dispatch exactly two sub-agents in parallel:
1. explore 0 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): One explore sub-agent inspects the HR schema and runs one compact server-side department aggregate over the full employee table for exactly seven departments: count and raw averages for job satisfaction, performance rating and work-life balance. It returns alphabetical rows, company controls and query provenance only; no employee rows or writes.
2. coder 0 (external-workflow-operator 0): One coder is the sole owner of Employee Engagement Survey. Call create_form once, add exactly five questions in order: 1-10 role satisfaction choice, five-option work-life choice, four-option career growth choice, 1-5 manager support choice, Yes/Maybe/No recommendation choice; then get_form once. Never retry create after ambiguity.

After Wave 1, the main agent computes rounded department indices, writes/runs the required Python analysis, and freezes seven rows, arithmetic mean of the seven rounded indices, highest/lowest, Above/Below classifications (deterministic equality rule), and one recommendation per department naming its lowest of the three metrics.

Wave 2 — dispatch exactly three coder sub-agents in parallel:
1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Sole writer of Employee_Engagement_Report.xlsx with exact Department_Scores, Survey_Design, Action_Items, alphabetical departments, literal numbers and full read-back.
2. coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 1): Sole owner of exactly one Notion page HR Engagement Dashboard. Fully paginate exact-title search, reuse one or create once, block on duplicates, write all seven department names/counts/indices and retrieve the page.
3. coder 2 (external-workflow-operator 2): Sole owner of the hr-leadership@company.com email with exact subject Employee Engagement Analysis Report and frozen highest/lowest findings. Paginate Sent search/read candidates, send at most once, and read back.

All writers self-verify; the main agent compares compact receipts only and launches no repair wave.
